'''Daniel Richard Green Jr.''' (born June 22, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. In his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] career, Green played for six teams. As of 2025, Green is one of just four players in history to have won NBA championships with three different teams; he won titles with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in [[2014 NBA Finals|2014]], the [[Toronto Raptors]] in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]], and the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]].

Green spent his college basketball career at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]] (UNC) from 2005 to 2009. He played in more games (145) and had more wins (123) than any [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|Tar Heel]] before him. In [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|2009]], during his senior year at UNC, Green won an [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA championship]].

Green was selected by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]]. After being waived by the Cavaliers, Green played for the San Antonio Spurs, the Reno Bighorns of the NBA Developmental League, and [[KK Olimpija]] in Slovenia. Green became a starting guard for the Spurs during the 2011–2012 season and remained with the Spurs until 2018. During the [[2013 NBA Finals]], Green set an NBA record for most [[three-point field goals]] made in a Finals series (23). He then won an NBA championship with the San Antonio Spurs in 2014. Known for his perimeter defense, Green was selected to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] in the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]]. In 2019, he won a second NBA championship in his only season with the Toronto Raptors. Green won a third championship in 2020 with the Los Angeles Lakers. He also played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].

==High school career==
As a high school freshman, Green attended [[North Babylon Union Free School District|North Babylon High School]] in [[North Babylon, New York]], on [[Long Island]] and in addition to basketball, he played [[quarterback]] on the [[High school football|football]] team. From his sophomore year onwards, Green attended [[St. Mary's High School (Manhasset, New York)|St. Mary's High School]], a private school, in [[Manhasset, New York]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Chan |first=Lorne |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/persistence-danny-green |title=The Persistence of Danny Green |work=NBA.com |date=July 14, 2015 |access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref> He averaged 20 points, 10 rebounds, 4 assists and 4 blocks as a senior. Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Green was listed as the No. 8 shooting guard and the No. 31 player in the nation in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/kevin-mccaskill-24887?view=pv|title=Kevin McCaskill, 2006 Offensive Center, South Florida|website=rivals.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Green came off the bench as the [[sixth man]] during his [[2005–06 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|freshman year at UNC]]. He averaged 5.2 points and 2.8 rebounds in his [[2006–07 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|sophomore season]].<ref name="ESPN college profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3988/type/mens-college-basketball |title=Danny Green Stats |work=ESPN.com |accessdate=April 28, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428155033/https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3988/type/mens-college-basketball |archive-date=April 28, 2022}}</ref> After his second year at North Carolina, Green considered transferring, but would ultimately finish his college career there.<ref name=":0"/>
[[File:Danny Green dance Senior Day.jpg|thumb|left|Green at UNC in 2009]]
In Green's [[2007–08 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|junior year]], he averaged 11.5 points, 4.9 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.9 turnovers, 1.2 steals, 1.2 blocks in 22.3 minutes per game. He also improved his true shooting percentage (TS%) significantly, increasing his field goal percentage to 46.9% and his free throw percentage to 87.3%. He shot 37.3% from the three-point line.<ref name="ESPN college profile"/>

Approaching his [[2008–09 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|senior season]], Green declared himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]]. However, he refrained from signing with an agent so that he had the option to return to school, which he decided to do on June 16, 2008.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/green_danny00.html |title=Player Bio: Danny Green |work=tarheelblue.cstv.com |publisher=[[University of North Carolina]] |accessdate=April 20, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090917024408/http://tarheelblue.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/green_danny00.html |archive-date=September 17, 2009}}</ref> He was named team captain alongside [[Bobby Frasor]] and [[Tyler Hansbrough]] for the year,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://northcarolina.scout.com/2/857249.html |title=No Decision Yet for Lawson, Ellington |first=Greg |last=Barnes |work=Scout.com |date=April 16, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401164524/http://northcarolina.scout.com/2/857249.html |archive-date=April 1, 2012}} InsideCarolina.com, The Independent Voice of UNC sports, April 16, 2009.</ref> and started every game as the Tar Heels [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|won their fifth national championship]].<ref name="College Sports Ref">{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/danny-green-1.html |title=Danny Green College Stats |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |accessdate=April 28, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027233354/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/danny-green-1.html |archive-date=October 27, 2021}}</ref> Green averaged 13.1 points, 4.7 rebounds, 2.7 assists, 1.7 turnovers, 1.8 steals and 1.3 blocks in 27.4 minutes per game for the season, again improving his shooting percentages, averaging 47.1% and 41.8% from the field and three-point line, respectively.<ref name="ESPN college profile"/>
Green was selected to the All-ACC third team,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/all-acc.html |title=All-Atlantic Coast Conference Winner |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |accessdate=April 28, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305012137/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/all-acc.html |archive-date=March 5, 2021}}</ref> and the ACC's All-Defensive Team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/acc-all-defense.html |title=Atlantic Coast Conference All-Defensive Winner |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |accessdate=April 28, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306010538/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/awards/acc-all-defense.html |archive-date=March 6, 2021}}</ref> He ended his college career with 1,368 points for the Tar Heels,<ref name="College Sports Ref"/> and held the school's all-time record for wins, with 123.<ref>{{cite book |title=One Fantastic Ride: The Inside Story of Carolina Basketball's 2009 Championship Season |first1=Adam |last1=Lucas |first2=Steve |last2=Kirschner |first3=Matt |last3=Bowers |publisher=[[University of North Carolina Press]] |year=2009 |page=240 |isbn=9780807833858}}</ref> Green played in more games (145) than any [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|Tar Heel]] before him. As of 2009, Green was also the only player in the history of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) with at least 1,000 points, 500 rebounds, 250 assists, 150 three-pointers, 150 blocks and 150 steals.<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Lemire|title=Doing the little things, UNC's Green makes his dad, teammates proud|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/joe_lemire/04/03/danny.green/1.html|website=SportsIllustrated.cnn.com |date=April 3, 2009|access-date=June 23, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024231248/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/joe_lemire/04/03/danny.green/1.html|archive-date=October 24, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cleveland Cavaliers (2009–2010)===
[[File:Danny Green warms up 20090930-6130.jpg|thumb|Danny Green with the Cleveland Cavaliers in November 2009]]
The [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] selected Green as the 46th overall pick of the [[2009 NBA draft]]. After he played in 20 games in his rookie year with the Cavaliers, the team waived Green at the beginning of the next season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/6ixfacts-dannygreen|title=6ix Quick Facts: Danny Green|website=NBA.com|date=September 10, 2018|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2010)===
Green was picked up by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on November 17, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_danny_green_101117.html |title=Spurs Sign Danny Green |work=NBA.com |date=2010-10-19 |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref> The Spurs waived him six days later after he appeared in two games.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs Waive Danny Green |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_waive_danny_green_101123.html |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=November 23, 2010 |access-date=2010-11-23}}</ref>

===Reno Bighorns (2011)===
In January 2011, Green was acquired by the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]]. He averaged 20 points, a team high, and 7.5 rebounds in 16 games with the Bighorns.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.mysanantonio.com/spursnation/2011/03/15/spurs-sign-swing-man-danny-green/ |title=Spurs Nation » Spurs sign swing man Danny Green |publisher=Blog.mysanantonio.com |date=2011-03-15 |access-date=2013-06-23 |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805133919/http://blog.mysanantonio.com/spursnation/2011/03/15/spurs-sign-swing-man-danny-green/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to San Antonio (2011)===
The Spurs signed Green again in March 2011,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blog.mysanantonio.com/spursnation/2011/03/15/spurs-sign-swing-man-danny-green/ |title=Spurs sign swing man Danny Green |publisher=Blog.mysanantonio.com |date=2011-03-15 |access-date=2013-06-23 |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805133919/http://blog.mysanantonio.com/spursnation/2011/03/15/spurs-sign-swing-man-danny-green/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> assigned him to the [[Austin Toros]] of the NBA Development League on April 2, and then recalled him on April 3.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/green_110402.html |title=Spurs Assign Danny Green To Austin Toros |work=NBA.com |date=2011-04-02 |access-date=2013-06-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131208185546/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/green_110402.html |archive-date=December 8, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Olimpija (2011)===
In August 2011, Green signed a one-year contract with [[KK Union Olimpija]], which included an NBA-out clause option when the [[2011 NBA lockout]] ended.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/adriatic-league/30414/danny_green_moves_to_union_olimpija.html |title=Danny Green moves to Union Olimpija |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref>

===Third stint with Spurs (2011–2018)===
====2011–13: Playoff upsets====
Green returned to the Spurs in 2011 after the lockout ended. Green had a breakout 2011–2012 season, starting 38 of his 66 games played and averaging 9.1 ppg. Green became the starting shooting guard for the Spurs when [[Manu Ginóbili]] returned to being the sixth man in the rotation. After the season, Green finished ninth in the league in voting for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]].<ref>{{cite news |date=May 4, 2012 |title=Magic's Ryan Anderson wins Kia Most Improved Player Award |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/04/most-improved-player/index.html |url-status=dead |access-date=2012-05-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508085354/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/04/most-improved-player/index.html |archive-date=May 8, 2012}}</ref>

On July 11, 2012, Green re-signed with the Spurs for $12 million over three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120711_green |title=Spurs Re-Sign Danny Green |work=NBA.com |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref> In his first game of the season, he scored 9 points and added 2 blocks in San Antonio's win over the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. On November 1, 2012, he scored 13 points in a win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. Then on November 3, Green scored 21 points to help the Spurs beat the [[Utah Jazz]] in a 110–100 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121103/UTASAS/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Spurs 110, Jazz 100 |work=NBA.com |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref> On November 13, 2012, he hit a game-winner against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], finishing the game with 11 points. On February 6, 2013, Green recorded career highs of 28 points and 8 three-pointers made in a win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He was one three-point field goal shy of [[Chuck Person]]'s record for most three-pointers made in a single game as a Spur.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130206/SASMIN/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Spurs 104, Timberwolves 94 |work=NBA.com |access-date=2013-06-23}}</ref>

In game 2 of the [[2013 NBA Finals]], Green was perfect from the field, including 5–5 from the three-point line. However, the Spurs lost in a blowout to the [[Miami Heat]], 103–84.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400467334|title=Heat ride Mario Chalmers in second half, cruise by Spurs in Game 2|date=June 9, 2013|access-date=2013-06-17|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> In game 3 of the NBA Finals, Green hit 7–9 from three-point range, including the one to set a Finals record for most three-pointers in a game by a team. He notched 27 total points in the Spurs' blowout 113–77 victory as the team took a 2–1 series lead in the process.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400467335|title=Spurs hit NBA Finals-record 16 3-pointers in rout of Heat|date=June 11, 2013|access-date=2013-06-17|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> On June 16 in game 5, Green made six three-pointers for a total of 25 in the series to that point, breaking the record for an NBA Finals series previously held by [[Ray Allen]], who made 22 in six games with the [[Boston Celtics]] in [[2008 NBA Finals|2008]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400467337|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819122818/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400467337|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 19, 2016|title=Manu Ginóbili's surprise start sparks Spurs, pushes Heat to brink|date=June 16, 2013|access-date=2013-06-17|work=ESPN.com}}</ref> By the end of the series, Green had made 27 three-pointers, but the Spurs lost the series in seven games. The record was later broken by [[Stephen Curry]] in [[2016 NBA Finals|2016]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Young|first1=Royce|title=Danny Green breaks NBA Finals 3-point record|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/danny-green-breaks-nba-finals-3-point-record/|website=CBS Sports|access-date=September 18, 2016|date=June 16, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Garcia|first1=Paul|title=Green's 3-Point Finals Record broken by Curry in Game 6 of 2016 Finals|url=http://projectspurs.com/2016-articles/greens-3-point-finals-record-broken-by-curry-in-game-6-of-2016-finals.html|website=Project Spurs|access-date=September 18, 2016|date=June 16, 2016|archive-date=October 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161006061644/http://projectspurs.com/2016-articles/greens-3-point-finals-record-broken-by-curry-in-game-6-of-2016-finals.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====2013–18: First championship and final years with Spurs====
On April 11, 2014, Green scored a career-high 33 points in a 112–104 win over the Phoenix Suns.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140411/PHXSAS/gameinfo.html Notebook: Spurs 110, Suns 104]</ref> On June 15, 2014, Green won his first NBA championship after the Spurs defeated the [[Miami Heat]] 4 games to 1 in the [[2014 NBA Finals]]. In doing so, Green joined [[Michael Jordan]] and [[James Worthy]] as the third Tar Heel to win both the NCAA and NBA championship.

On December 19, 2014, Green scored a season-high 27 points in the 119–129 triple overtime loss to the Portland Trail Blazers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141219/PORSAS/gameinfo.html |title=Lillard scores 43 as Blazers beat Spurs in 3 OT |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610115228/http://www.nba.com/games/20141219/PORSAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 10, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On April 12, 2015, Green recorded 3 three-pointers against the Phoenix Suns to set a franchise record for the most three-pointers in a season at 191.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150412/PHXSAS/gameinfo.html Duncan leads Spurs to 11th straight win, 107–91 over Suns]</ref>

On July 14, 2015, Green re-signed with the Spurs<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs Re-Sign Danny Green|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-re-sign-danny-green|access-date=July 14, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2015}}</ref> to a reported four-year, $45 million contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/spurs/2015/07/01/danny-green-4-year-deal-spurs/29563997/|title=Danny Green agrees to 4-year contract with Spurs|publisher=osatoday.com|author=Sam Amick|date=2015-07-01|access-date=2015-07-01}}</ref> On January 6, 2016, Green hit two three-pointers against the Utah Jazz, giving him 662 with San Antonio to surpass [[Bruce Bowen]] (661) for second in franchise history.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160106/UTASAS/gameinfo.html |title=Duncan scores 18, Spurs rout Jazz to move to 21–0 at home |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 7, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704130607/http://www.nba.com/games/20160106/UTASAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=July 4, 2018 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 9, 2016, Green made his season debut for San Antonio, scoring eight points against the Houston Rockets in his return from a strained left quadriceps.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899564|title=Rockets 101-99 Spurs (Nov 9, 2016) Game Recap|website=ESPN}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/kawhi-leonard-and-danny-green-named-nba-all-defensive-teams|title=KAWHI LEONARD AND DANNY GREEN NAMED TO NBA ALL-DEFENSIVE TEAMS|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2017|access-date=June 27, 2017}}</ref>

On December 28, 2017, against the [[New York Knicks]], Green became the 127th player in league history to reach 900 career three-pointers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975265|title=Aldridge leads Spurs' charge past Knicks, 119–107|work=ESPN.com|date=December 28, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2017}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2018–2019)===
[[File:1 danny green toronto raptors 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Green in 2019]]
On July 18, 2018, Green and teammate [[Kawhi Leonard]] were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[DeMar DeRozan]], [[Jakob Pöltl]] and a protected 2019 first round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/kawhitrade-071818|title=Toronto Raptors Acquire Kawhi Leonard|work=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2018|access-date=July 18, 2018}}</ref> On November 10, 2018, in a 128–112 win over the [[New York Knicks]], Green reached 1,000 three-pointers for his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070855|title=Siakam scores career-high 23, Raptors beat Knicks 128–112|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2018|access-date=November 10, 2018}}</ref> On December 14, he had 19 points and 11 rebounds while matching his season high with five three-pointers in a 128–122 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071108|title=Lillard scores 24, Blazers hold off NBA-best Raptors 128–122|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2018}}</ref> On January 19, he had a season-high 24 points and set a franchise record for three-pointers in a quarter with seven in the third, as the Raptors beat the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] 119–90. With 21 points in the third, he fell one shy of [[Kyle Lowry]]'s franchise record for a quarter. Green also matched a career high with eight threes for the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071360|title=Green hits 7 3s in 3rd quarter, Raptors top Grizzlies 119–90|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2019|access-date=January 19, 2019}}</ref> On April 1, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 121–109 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071829|title=Green scores season-high 29 as Raptors beat Magic 121–109|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2019|access-date=April 2, 2019}}</ref> Green helped the Raptors reach the [[2019 NBA Finals]], where they defeated the [[Golden State Warriors]] in six games, with Green earning his second NBA championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401134820|title=Raptors capture first NBA title, beat Warriors in Game 6|work=ESPN.com|date=June 13, 2019|access-date=June 13, 2019}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2019–2020)===
The [[Los Angeles Lakers]] signed Green to a two-year $30 million contract on July 6, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/190706-lakers-sign-cook-cousins-green|title=Lakers Sign Quinn Cook, DeMarcus Cousins, and Danny Green|website=Los Angeles Lakers|language=en|access-date=2019-07-07}}</ref> He debuted for the Lakers on October 22, 2019, where he led the team with 28 points in 32 minutes on 10-of-14 [[Field goal (basketball)|field goal makes]] and 7-of-9 three-point makes in a 112–102 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. His 28 points are the most points in a debut in franchise history, breaking [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]]'s record of 27 points.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401160624|title=Lakers vs. Clippers – Box Score – October 22, 2019 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-10-23}}</ref>

Green contributed to the Lakers finishing as the top seed in the Western Conference in a shortened season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] that [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|suspended the season]] for four months. The Lakers reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], where they defeated the [[Miami Heat]] 4–2 to win the 2020 NBA championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30096209 |quote=...before defeating the Portland Trail Blazers, Houston Rockets and Denver Nuggets in five games each and the Heat in six.|title=Los Angeles Lakers lean on defense in dominant Game 6 win vs. Miami Heat, claim first NBA title in a decade|work=ESPN|date=October 12, 2020}}</ref> Green and teammate [[LeBron James]] became the third and fourth players in league history to win a championship with three different teams, joining [[John Salley]] and [[Robert Horry]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/in/los-angeles-lakers/news/nba-finals-2020-lebron-james-and-danny-green-join-exclusive-list-of-players-to-win-championships-with-three-different-teams/2k44d51hll6m11atm4bf9qpnl|title=NBA Finals 2020: LeBron James and Danny Green join exclusive club in winning three championships with three different teams|date=January 13, 2022|website=www.sportingnews.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kidane |first1=Benyam |title=NBA Finals 2020: LeBron James and Danny Green join exclusive club in winning three championships with three different teams |url=https://in.nba.com/news/nba-finals-2020-lebron-james-and-danny-green-join-exclusive-list-of-players-to-win-championships-with-three-different-teams/2k44d51hll6m11atm4bf9qpnl |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=October 12, 2020}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)===
On November 18, 2020, Green, along with the draft rights to [[Jaden McDaniels]], was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Dennis Schröder]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers Acquire Dennis Schröder |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-acquire-dennis-schroder |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=November 18, 2020}}</ref> On December 8, Green, [[Terrance Ferguson]] and [[Vincent Poirier]] were traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for [[Al Horford]], the draft rights of [[Théo Maledon]] and [[Vasilije Micić]], and a 2025 first-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Team Acquires Green, Ferguson, and Poirier |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-acquires-green-ferguson-and-poirier |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 8, 2020 |date=December 8, 2020}}</ref>

On August 7, 2021, Green re-signed with the 76ers on a two-year, $20 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=76ers Re-Sign Danny Green|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-re-sign-danny-green|access-date=2021-08-09|website=Philadelphia 76ers|language=en}}</ref> On May 12, 2022, during game 6 of the 76ers' second-round series against the [[Miami Heat]], Green suffered a left knee injury in a 99–90 loss, due to a collision with his teammate [[Joel Embiid]]. The next day, he was diagnosed with a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) and [[Fibular collateral ligament|lateral collateral ligament]] (LCL) in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia 76ers forward Danny Green suffered torn ACL, LCL in season-ending loss to Miami Heat |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33910720 |access-date=March 26, 2023 |website=ESPN|date=May 13, 2022 }}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2022–2023)===
During the [[2022 NBA draft]], Green, along with the draft rights to [[David Roddy]], were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[De'Anthony Melton]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire draft rights to David Roddy and Danny Green from Philadelphia 76ers |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-draft-rights-to-david-roddy-and-danny-green-from-philadelphia-76ers-220624 |website=NBA.com |access-date=June 27, 2022 |date=June 24, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies trade De'Anthony Melton to 76ers for 23rd pick, selects David Roddy|url=https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2022/6/23/23181078/memphis-grizzlies-trade-deanthony-melton-to-76ers-for-23rd-pick-selects-david-roddy-nba-draft-2022|website=SB Nation|access-date=June 23, 2022|date=June 23, 2022|archive-date=November 28, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221128203441/https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2022/6/23/23181078/memphis-grizzlies-trade-deanthony-melton-to-76ers-for-23rd-pick-selects-david-roddy-nba-draft-2022|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 1, 2023, Green made his Grizzlies debut, putting up three points in 10 minutes played in a 122–112 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/lists/multiple-sixers-react-to-danny-green-making-grizzlies-debut-acl-recovery/|title=Multiple Sixers react to Danny Green making Grizzlies debut, ACL recovery|website=USA TODAY|last=Carlin|first=Ky|date=February 2, 2023|access-date=February 2, 2023}}</ref>

===Return to Cleveland (2023)===
On February 9, 2023, Green was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Complete Three-Team Trade with the L.A. Clippers and Memphis Grizzlies|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-three-team-trade-with-the-l-a-clippers-and-memphis-grizzlies|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> He and the Rockets agreed to a contract buyout three days later, and he was subsequently waived.<ref>{{cite web|title=Danny Green, John Wall officially waived by Houston|url=https://hoopshype.com/2023/02/12/danny-green-john-wall-officially-waived-by-houston/|website=HoopsHype.com|date=February 12, 2023|access-date=February 12, 2023|archive-date=March 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230319135520/https://hoopshype.com/2023/02/12/danny-green-john-wall-officially-waived-by-houston/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On February 15, 2023, Green signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavs add veteran swingman Danny Green|url=https://www.nba.com/news/cavs-sign-danny-green|website=NBA.com|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023}}</ref> He made his Cavaliers debut the same day, scoring three points in a 118–112 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Kevin|last=Cooney|title=EMBIID HAS 29 POINTS, HELPS 76ERS SNAP CAVALIERS' WIN STREAK|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200875|website=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}}</ref>

===Second stint with 76ers (2023)===
On September 13, 2023, Green signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Danny Green Signs with the 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-danny-green|website=NBA.com|date=September 13, 2023|access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref> On November 1, he was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Three-Team Deal with LA Clippers, Oklahoma City Thunder Completed|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-trade-harden-tucker-to-clippers|website=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2023|access-date=November 1, 2023}}</ref> 

On October 10, 2024, Green announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite news|first=Tim|last=Reynolds|title=Danny Green, a 3-time NBA champion, announces his retirement|url=https://www.nba.com/news/danny-green-a-3-time-nba-champion-announces-his-retirement|website=NBA.com|date=October 10, 2024|access-date=October 10, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:Danny Green(1).jpg|thumb|Green with the [[Toronto Raptors]]]]
===Family===
Green's brother, Rashad, played for [[Manhattan College]] in 2007–08 and the [[San Francisco Dons|University of San Francisco]] from 2009 to 2012.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/37416/ Rashad Green]. [[ESPN.com]]</ref> His younger brother, [[Devonte Green]], played for [[Indiana University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/danny-green-confident-brother-devonte-will-thrive-at-indiana-c37870 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819114638/http://www.newsday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/danny-green-confident-brother-devonte-will-thrive-at-indiana-1.11315608 |url-status=live |archive-date=August 19, 2016 |title=Danny Green confident brother Devonte will thrive at Indiana}}</ref> His second cousins are professional players [[Gerald Green]] and [[Garlon Green]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120715133028/http://usfdons.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/081408aaa.html|title="USF Men's Basketball Announces Signing of Rashad Green,"}} USF official website, August 14, 2008.</ref> A first cousin, Jordan Green, played for [[Texas A&M University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://12thman.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jordan-green/2890 |title=Jordan Green - Men's Basketball |website=Texas A&M Athletics - 12thMan.com}}</ref> A third cousin, [[Willie Green]], played for the [[Detroit Mercy Titans men's basketball|University of Detroit Mercy]] and then in the NBA, and later became the head coach of [[New Orleans Pelicans]].
In 2020, Green got engaged to his longtime girlfriend, Blair Bashen.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/nba/lakers/news/she-said-yes-danny-green-got-engaged-to-longtime-girlfriend |title=She Said Yes! Danny Green Got Engaged To Longtime Girlfriend |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 17, 2020}}</ref> The two were married in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Danny Green's Wedding Was Utterly Insane |url=https://www.thebiglead.com/posts/danny-green-wedding-blair-bashen-video-01fddpp7vqm6 |access-date=2021-08-19 |website=The Big Lead |date=August 18, 2021}}</ref>

===Podcast===
In 2018, Green and longtime friend and sports broadcaster Harrison Sanford launched a podcast entitled "Inside the Green Room".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/qa-inside-green-room-podcast-co-host-harrison-sanford/ |title=Q&A: Inside the Green Room podcast co-host Harrison Sanford |last=Loung |first=Steven |date=September 4, 2018 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=June 25, 2019}}</ref> While they intended to start with a soft launch in the summer of 2018, Green was traded to the Toronto Raptors just prior to recording what was to be the pilot episode, so they decided to do a full launch with the first episode.<ref name=":1"/> The podcast gained sponsorship from Yahoo Sports Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.insidegreenroom.com/ |title=Inside the Green Room |website=Inside the Green Room |access-date=June 25, 2019 |archive-date=November 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112014538/https://www.insidegreenroom.com/ |url-status=dead}}</ref> Episodes have featured players and coaches from the Toronto Raptors, as well as players from other teams and other sports journalists. Green has expressed an interest in moving into sports broadcasting after his playing career is over.<ref name=":1"/><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.closeup360.com/business/danny-green-dishes-on-podcasting-puma-hoops-and-nba-all-star-weekend/ |title=Raptors Guard Danny Green Dishes on Podcasting, PUMA Hoops and NBA All-Star Weekend |last=Davies |first=Spencer |date=February 15, 2019 |website=Closeup 360 |access-date=June 25, 2019 |archive-date=January 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127160143/https://www.closeup360.com/business/danny-green-dishes-on-podcasting-puma-hoops-and-nba-all-star-weekend/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>
